utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, good afternoon to everybody. Madam Registrar -- Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-99-36-A, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I should first do what every judge customarily does, and that is to test out the audio equipment. And so I shall ask whether everybody hears me. Mr. Brdjanin, do you hear me in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes, I can hear you in a language I understand, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: There are two appeals, one by the Prosecution, one by the Defence. And I think the Prosecution goes first; is that right, Mr. Ackerman? So I shall call for the appearances on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mathias Marcussen appearing with Lourdes Galicia for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And then the appearances on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm John Ackerman. I'm here on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin, along with Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We have made an order admitting the brief from amicus curiae. Is there any appearance for the amicus curiae, or need we concern ourselves at this time? The consensus of the bar?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think we need not concern ourselves, Your Honour. They have applied for an extension and received it, and will be filing in due course, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So the consensus of the bar is that we need not bother about them. Now, this is a status conference. A scheduling order for the purpose was issued on the 27th of May. This is the second status conference to be ordered in this case. The first was held on the 3rd of February, and the second should have been on the 3rd of June, because, under the law, a status conference has to be held every 120 days, but Defence counsel had some professional difficulties and the accused waived his right to insist on a status conference being held strictly in accordance with the Rules and so we have appointed today as a date for hearing this appeal, rather, as a date for this conference. Now, the purpose of the conference is set out in Rule 65 bis(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. We read them out on the last occasion. Is there need for these -- this rule to be read again? No. So the Rule, then, concerns two questions. One is whether the appellant, Mr. Brdjanin, has any concerns as regards his conditions of detention, and the second has to do with an updating which the Court should give as to the status of the appeal. Now, then, Mr. Ackerman, are there any concerns that your client would like to present to the Court at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: None that he's expressed to me, Your Honour. I think there are none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, then, I see a sign of concurrence from behind you on the part of Mr. Brdjanin. Now, you agree with that, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the updating is very simple. The judgement in this case was given on the 1st of September last year. The Prosecution then filed its notice of appeal on the 30th of September, and Mr. Brdjanin followed suit the next day, the 1st of October. The Prosecution then presented its brief on the 28th of January. Mr. Brdjanin's response to that brief was filed on the 10th of May. The Prosecution replied to that response on the 25th of May this year. So, the pleading procedure for the appeal by the Prosecution looks to me as if it's concluded; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, save the issue that was raised with respect to the amicus curiae.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And our possibility of maybe responding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We can come to that. You have filed a recent motion on that issue, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in our response to the amicus's request for an extension of time we raised this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then I come to Mr. Brdjanin's appeal. He applied for leave to file a supplementary notice of appeal on the 20th of May this year and so that application was granted a few days later, on the 3rd of June this year - That's last week, last week Thursday, or Friday - and his appeal brief is accordingly due on the 27th of June this year. Now, a question has been raised as to whether the physical perpetrators in a crime must be members of the JCE and this has led to some special pleading on the point. Very briefly, I think the Defence took the position that they were not terribly interested in this area and so with a view to securing some adversarial input in the matter, an amicus brief was order and leave was given to the association of Defence lawyers to file an amicus brief. 30 days were granted and a 15-page limit was affixed and that order will then expire on the 5th of June. Yesterday. Yesterday. An extension was granted on the 3rd of June to the 5th of July next month. So in sum, we have this position: that Mr. Brdjanin's appeal brief is to be expected on the 27th of June this year, and the Prosecution would then have a right to reply to that. So the appeal process there is ongoing. And then we come to the amicus brief. I think this was first ordered by the 5th of July and -- yes. There was an extension granted to the 5th of July so they have up to the 5th of July to file their brief, and accordingly, the pleadings stage of the case is still ongoing. The Prosecution has asked to reply to the amicus brief. That doesn't terribly concern you, Mr. Ackerman. So those are the things I have to say. Would you like to say anything, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Not at this stage, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then I turn to Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have a couple of things. Sometimes I'm not as precise as I would like to be in the things that I write and I wouldn't want the impression to persist that I am not interested in the JCE issue. I'm academically very interested in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What I was trying to say in my maybe inartfully drafted pleading, Your Honour, was that I thought the issue would be death with better if it was in an adversarial proceeding where both parties really had a legitimate interest in the outcome. If you look at my brief, however, you'll see that I actually briefed it fairly thoroughly, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I haven't got a practical interest in this case. Is that one way of putting it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is that one way of putting it, to say that you do not have a practical interest in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah, the outcome of that issue cannot affect my current client. It could affect a future client, so I do have that academic interest. The other thing I wanted to basically inquire of you about: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Because of the approval of the additional grounds of appeal, we really haven't done anything about a scheduling with regard to the briefing with regard to those grounds. And what I would like to inquire, Your Honour, is whether or not Your Honour would be receptive to a pleading from me that requests the filing date for the appellant's brief to be advanced another few days, perhaps into middle to late July, so that it could be a consolidated brief including not only the original grounds of appeal but the supplemental that have just been approved. So that way I could file not one but -- if that would be something that you would consider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let me understand you. At the moment your time limit is when?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: June 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: June 27. And would you like July?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Somewhere between the 15th and 25th of July, somewhere in that neighbourhood. That way I could file a consolidated brief with all of the points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let me try to discover what might be the reaction of the Prosecution to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Brdjanin now has in the neighbourhood of 180 grounds of appeal and we agreed to the addition of the new 20 grounds of appeal. So we would not -- we would not object to an extension of time. But I would like to just express a concern that is coming up on the part of the Prosecution in this regard. That is that the schedule had moved along so for us it is posing a problem in terms of practical its and having staff available to respond. So depending on what the eventual schedule might be we might be seeking an extension of time to file our response brief. Nothing excessive, but it has been difficult for us for timing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Response brief to Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: To Mr. Ackerman's brief. It's simply is that -- as the scheduling of the briefing in this appeal has moved from initially being us having to respond during May and June, it has now been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Do you have the feeling that this schedule is unravelling before our eyes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think that it would not be something that would cause concern overall. We would have a number of issues that needs to be dealt with any way. So the Prosecution is not concerned with the overall length of the appeal. I would just like to inform the Chamber that maybe we would be needing an extension of time but we don't object to the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, you're sitting pretty. The Prosecution doesn't object but what I suggest is this: that you leave the matter for the responsible authorities in the chambers to decide in the normal way, bearing in mind both what you have said and what the prosecuting counsel has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think what you're saying is go ahead and file a motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: File a motion and see what comes out of it. We mightn't agree to the full extent of what you have asked for. We might pare it down. What we have to bear in mind is this: That it's not really a question of applying the rules just because they are there, but it's a question of good order and discipline in the hearing procedures relating to all appeals.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I can assure Your Honour that I've been working very diligently and this is just a very, very huge appeal with that many grounds of appeal and the number of issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 180 at this point. Some of those I will abandon in the course of preparing because I'm finding they overlap a little bit but -- so some of the grounds, what you'll see is I'll just refer back to writing earlier in the brief on the issue. But there is still a huge number of matters that need to be considered. This was a trial that lasted for 27 months and it's not -- this is not a simple matter. It's a very complicated matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand that rules are rules but by the same token I think the Rules were made for the average case here and I think this case is a bit extraordinary and deserves, perhaps, extraordinary treatment. That's why I even raised the matter, Your Honour. Otherwise I wouldn't raise it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Good point. We will look at that when it comes. Any other points, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that's all, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It's a very good thing that we have this Rule that brings the two sides together in front of the Court, and it gives to the accused, the appellant, Mr. Brdjanin, an opportunity to know the score of things. So if there is no other business at this time, we will take the adjournment. All right?
